claims.text: Machine-learning methods, specifically deep learning, are the proposed intervention.
Deep learning will improve the accuracy of determining the listed melting and liquid-state thermodynamic properties relative to traditional experimental and computational methods.
Deep learning will improve the availability of the listed melting and liquid-state thermodynamic properties relative to traditional methods.
Deep learning will improve the efficiency of determining the listed melting and liquid-state thermodynamic properties relative to traditional methods.
The target material system consists of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The intervention is intended to operate across a large compositional space.
The intervention applies to high-temperature solid and liquid states of high-entropy alloys.
Configurational entropy structurally mediates the effect of deep learning on thermodynamic-property determination.
Lattice distortion structurally mediates the effect of deep learning on thermodynamic-property determination.
Dislocation motion structurally mediates the effect of deep learning on thermodynamic-property determination.
Machine-learning models can efficiently predict high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties by learning patterns from existing data.
Traditional computational methods have limited accuracy for predicting melting temperature.
The quality and quantity of training data may affect machine-learning performance.
The choice of algorithm and model may affect machine-learning performance.
